feed.title: Icons, Photos & Illustration — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome GIF
entry.content:
A list of tools and resources for the GIF animated-image format. Unlike general image lists, it gathers only tools for creating, optimising and playing GIFs.

https://github.com/davisonio/awesome-gif

entry.title: Awesome Icons
entry.content:
A list of downloadable SVG/PNG/font icon projects. Unlike a single icon set, it lays dozens of sets side by side so you can pick by style and licence.

https://github.com/notlmn/awesome-icons

entry.title: Awesome Pixel Art
entry.content:
A list of tools and resources for pixel-level digital art. Unlike general drawing lists, it focuses on pixel editors, palettes and pixel-art tutorials.

https://github.com/Siilwyn/awesome-pixel-art

entry.title: Feather Icons
entry.content:
A simple, consistent open-source icon set at a single stroke weight. Unlike large libraries it offers a minimal visual language and small file size.

https://feathericons.com/

entry.title: Flaticon
entry.content:
A vast icon bank offering millions of vector icons in various styles.

https://www.flaticon.com

entry.title: Font Awesome
entry.content:
The most widely used icon and logo library on the web. Unlike collecting SVGs one by one you add icons as a font/CSS class in a single line.

https://fontawesome.com/

entry.title: Gratisography
entry.content:
Unusual and creative free stock photos. Unlike archives such as Unsplash, its quirky, humorous shots steer clear of the clichéd stock-photo look.

https://gratisography.com/

entry.title: Haikei
entry.content:
A browser tool that generates blobs, waves and layered SVG background shapes. Unlike drawing SVG by hand, you generate random but controllable shapes in a click and export them.

https://haikei.app

entry.title: Hero Patterns
entry.content:
Repeatable SVG background patterns whose colour and opacity you tune, then copy the CSS. Unlike image-file backgrounds they are tiny and recolourable in CSS.

https://heropatterns.com

entry.title: Humaaans
entry.content:
A library of human illustrations whose parts you can mix and pose. Unlike ready illustrations you assemble the figure limb by limb into an original scene.

https://www.humaaans.com/

entry.title: IcoFont
entry.content:
2,100+ free icons to spice up designs, also usable as an icon font. Unlike downloading SVGs one by one, you drop an icon into a page with a CSS class.

https://icofont.com/

entry.title: Iconify
entry.content:
A library unifying 100+ icon sets under one API/component. Unlike installing each set separately you pull and mix them all from one interface.

https://iconify.design/

entry.title: iconmonstr
entry.content:
A site with 316 free icon collections, all by a single designer. Unlike marketplaces such as Iconfinder it keeps one consistent style, so icons from different collections still sit well together.

https://iconmonstr.com/

entry.title: Icons8
entry.content:
A broad asset source offering icons, illustrations, photos and music in various styles. Unlike single-type sites it gives many types in one consistent visual language.

https://icons8.com/

entry.title: Iconscout
entry.content:
A large collection bringing together icons, illustrations and 3D assets. Unlike sites offering a single asset type, it covers all of them under one search and licence; much of it is paid.

https://iconscout.com/

entry.title: IRA Design
entry.content:
Free illustrations with editable colours and objects. Unlike ready-made stock illustrations, you choose the gradient and objects to compose your own scene.

https://iradesign.io/illustrations

entry.title: LineIcons
entry.content:
A line-style icon set of 31,000+ icons, free and premium together; the full set needs a subscription. Unlike mixed-style sets, every icon shares the same stroke weight and style.

https://lineicons.com/

entry.title: Lorem Picsum
entry.content:
A service returning placeholder photos at any size (the lorem ipsum of images). Unlike fixed placeholders you pass a size in the URL and get a real photo.

https://picsum.photos/

entry.title: ManyPixels Gallery
entry.content:
A free illustration gallery with editable colour. Similar to unDraw; it offers a larger, topic-based collection and multiple formats.

https://www.manypixels.co/gallery

entry.title: Nappy
entry.content:
High-quality free photos of Black and Brown people. Unlike general stock archives it focuses on representation, surfacing images those archives lack.

https://www.nappy.co

entry.title: Open Peeps
entry.content:
Pablo Stanley’s hand-drawn, CC0 illustration library. Unlike ready-made illustrations, you build characters from parts — face, hair, outfit, pose.

https://www.openpeeps.com

entry.title: OpenMoji
entry.content:
An openly licensed emoji library in one design language. Unlike platform emojis it gives editable SVG emojis that look the same everywhere.

https://openmoji.org/

entry.title: Pexels
entry.content:
A stock source offering free photos and videos together. Unlike photo-only sites it also gives royalty-free video in the same interface.

https://www.pexels.com/

entry.title: Picjumbo
entry.content:
An archive of free and premium stock photos started by photographer Viktor Hanáček. Unlike Unsplash, one photographer’s style dominates, and there are paid premium packs too.

https://picjumbo.com/

entry.title: Pixabay
entry.content:
A royalty-free bank gathering photos, illustrations, vectors and video in one place. Unlike single-type sites it returns multi-format media in one search.

https://pixabay.com/

entry.title: Public Domain Archive
entry.content:
An archive of public-domain (copyright-free) stock photos. Unlike licensed free archives, the images are in the public domain: no attribution or licence terms apply.

https://www.publicdomainarchive.com/

entry.title: Remix Icon
entry.content:
A consistent open-source icon set coming in both line and solid styles. Unlike mixed sets every icon exists in both styles — consistency across a UI.

https://remixicon.com/

entry.title: StockSnap
entry.content:
Free stock photos with no attribution required, released under CC0. Unlike Unsplash’s own licence, CC0 leaves every use open, redistribution included.

https://stocksnap.io/

entry.title: Storyset
entry.content:
Freepik’s set of free, editable illustrations (Storyset); you can recolour them and download them animated. Unlike Freepik’s main archive, every image is customisable in the browser; free use requires attribution.

https://storyset.com/

entry.title: unDraw
entry.content:
An openly licensed illustration set whose colour you can change to your brand. Unlike fixed illustrations you switch the accent colour in one place and get a consistent set.

https://undraw.co/illustrations

entry.title: Unsplash
entry.content:
One of the largest free sources of high-resolution, royalty-free photographs. Unlike paid banks it is open to commercial use with no attribution required.

https://unsplash.com/

entry.title: Visual Hunt
entry.content:
A service searching millions of free stock images in one place, with search by colour. Unlike a single archive it searches several sources together; the trade-off is that the licence varies from image to image.

https://visualhunt.com/

entry.title: 3Dassets.one
entry.content:
A search engine that consolidates several 3D asset sites into one query, filterable by licence and price. Against visiting each site, the licence filter is the point — you can isolate what is actually usable commercially.

https://3dassets.one/

entry.title: ambientCG
entry.content:
An archive of CC0-licensed PBR textures and materials, shipping colour, normal, roughness and displacement maps together. Unlike most texture sites the licence really is CC0 — no attribution needed, commercial use fine.

https://cc0textures.com/

entry.title: Lucide
entry.content:
An icon library of over 1,600 SVG icons with ready packages for React, Vue and Svelte. It is the community fork of Feather, and the difference is that it kept growing while Feather went quiet — and that it tree-shakes down to the icons you import.

https://lucide.dev/

entry.title: The Noun Project
entry.content:
A searchable archive of millions of icons and symbols, with several visual takes on each concept. Unlike an icon library it is not a consistent set but a dictionary of concepts — the place where an icon for one very specific object actually exists.

https://thenounproject.com/

entry.title: Devicons
entry.content:
An icon font of programming language and tool logos, used as technology badges in CVs, slides and READMEs. Unlike general icon sets, it focuses solely on technology logos.

https://vorillaz.github.io/devicons/#/main

entry.title: LottieFiles
entry.content:
An archive and editor of lightweight JSON-based vector animations. Compared with GIF, it gives scalable, code-controllable motion at a fraction of the file size.

https://lottiefiles.com/

entry.title: Same Energy
entry.content:
Searches by visual similarity rather than keywords — you hand it an image and ask for more like it. Discovery through aesthetics, with no need to find the word first.

https://same.energy/
